ops.text: Flat rebuilds its child lists first, then preorder over them
ops.why: The rebuild followed the links twice (preorder, then the child lists, in preorder) with a subtree-size pass between. Now one pass over the slots builds the child lists (each sibling chain followed once, the lists in slot order), and a walk over those lists gives preorder and subtree ends, with no frame for a leaf. benches/forest.rs flat_rebuild, medians in one session: 100k nodes 338-343 us against 452-575 us, 10k 33-34 us against 43-57 us; the dirty walk is unchanged (it reads the same contiguous lists). Measured on the way, and why the cheap incremental idea was dropped: the child-list pass is about 35% of the rebuild (130 us at 100k) and the preorder walk 65%, so appending only the changed parents' lists would save little; the walk is what an incremental update has to avoid.

ops.body: A full rebuild is now about 340 us at 100k nodes and 33 us at 10k (8c89475), 65% of it the preorder walk. An incremental update has to avoid that walk: rebuild only the changed parents' subtree ranges, then shift what follows (positions and ends move by the size change, a memmove), falling back to a full rebuild when changed ranges overlap or the root list changed. Worth it once parda's passes show rebuilds in a frame budget; parda's own note (graft 01a10a6b, point 3) says the full rebuild is fine while structure changes only after reconciliation.
